items.title: Why pools smell like chlorine
items.summary: Why pools smell like chlorine. Mark Rober filled two buckets with clean water and four times the normal amount of chlorine, then added a tiny splash of pee to bucket B. A day later, bucket A smelled like water and bucket B smelled exactly like a pool. The CDC says that "chlorine" smell is probably chloramines, which form when chlorine combines with pee and sweat. Idea and experiment: Mark Rober. Source: CDC, Preventing Eye Irritation from Pool Chemicals (cdc.gov). Clips: Mark Rober, "How much pee is in a pool?" (YouTube Short); Pixabay footage by xat-ch, BernardMedia-DR, Vladvictoria, jcax2, olenailinska, Ian5152, stefaniejockschat, Coverr-Free-Footage, flutie8211, swistakens, MilanWulf. Send this to the friend who swears they've never peed in a pool. #Shorts #science #swimming #pool

items.title: Why your voice sounds weird on recordings
items.summary: Why your voice sounds weird on recordings. When you talk, sound reaches your ear through the air and through your skull. Bone carries frequencies up to about 1 kHz, so you sound deeper to yourself. A microphone only hears the air path. Source: JAIST (Unoki), Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research, 2021. Idea: ASAP SCIENCE. Clips: Daniel Thrasher, "When you hear your own voice for the first time" (YouTube); Pixabay footage by Engin_Akyurt, stevediaz, MrWashingt0n, intersubjektiv, magicmore, NeuroPixels, VFS_World, Bastien86, flutie8211, iwsky, conte_public, mephala1980. items.title: Why airplane windows have a tiny hole
items.summary: Why airplane windows have a tiny hole. Cruise altitude air is about 3.4 psi and the cabin is about 11, so each window is pushed outward with roughly 8 psi. The hole in the middle pane lets cabin air reach the outer pane, which carries the load. Sources: ScienceAlert (GKN Aerospace, American Vacuum Society), FAA 14 CFR 25.841. The company is developing a shared core for two products: Superpower, a natural-gas turbine for AI data centers, and Symphony, the engine intended for the Overture supersonic airliner. Blake explains why Boom decided to build its own engine and its plan to use turbine revenue and operating data to help develop Overture.
